question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)={x}^{2}(t)+2x(t)+y(t)-1 \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-2x(t)+3y(t)-{y}^{2}(t)-2\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of ODEs above. An equilibrium point of the system is $[0,\,1]^{T}.$ Which of the following is the system obtained by shifting this equilibrium to the origin?
question.worked_solution:
To shift the system's equilibrium from ${x}^{∗}$ to the origin, we define the deviation vector

$$
u=x-{x}^{∗},
$$

where $x=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]$ and $u=[\begin{aligned}u(t) \\ v(t)\end{aligned}].$

In our case, we have

$$
u=x-[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,⇒\,x=u+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,\text{and}\,{x}^{′}={u}^{′}.
$$

In coordinate form, this can be written as follows:

$$
x(t)=u(t),\,y(t)=v(t)+1,\,{x}^{′}(t)={u}^{′}(t),\,{v}^{′}(t)={y}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now substitute these into the given system.

- Substituting into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & ={x}^{2}(t)+2x(t)+y(t)-1 \\ {u}^{′}(t) & ={u}^{2}(t)+2u(t)+(v(t)+1)-1 \\  & ={u}^{2}(t)+2u(t)+v(t).\end{aligned}
$$

- Substituting into the second equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =-2x(t)+3y(t)-{y}^{2}(t)-2 \\ {v}^{′}(t) & =-2u(t)+3(v(t)+1)-(v(t)+1)^{2}-2 \\  & =-2u(t)+3v(t)+3-({v}^{2}(t)+2v(t)+1)-2 \\  & =-2u(t)+v(t)-{v}^{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the shifted system is the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{u}^{′}(t)={u}^{2}(t)+2u(t)+v(t) \\ {v}^{′}(t)=-2u(t)+v(t)-{v}^{2}(t)\end{aligned}
$$
